records.detail: src/excel_mcp/operations/protection.py:99 calls openpyxl SheetProtection.set_password(), which writes Excel's legacy sheet-protection hash into the workbook. It is not an account password and the project is not a Django app, so there is no password-strength validator to call.

docs/index.html:9 is <link rel="canonical" href="https://excelmcpserver.com/"> on the project's static landing page: a self-link, not a script or stylesheet load, so SRI does not apply (same shape as superdesigndev-treg).

Hand review; no tool rule covers it. The README 'Remote use' and 'Docker' examples set EXCEL_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN=change-me together with --host 0.0.0.0 / -p 8017:8017, and cli.py:42 accepts any non-empty value, so a copy-pasted command serves the network behind a token printed in the README. Not a vulnerability: the server refuses a non-loopback host with no token, and the value says to change it. Refusing the documented placeholder, or tokens shorter than about 16 characters, at startup would close the copy-paste path.
